overview.headline: Building emergency savings and learning the benefit of starting early

keyPoints.point: Students learn a good rule is to save 10 percent of earnings and keep three months of living expenses for emergencies.
keyPoints.quote: A good rule to live by is to save 10 percent of what you earn

keyPoints.point: Teens learn to track what they spend in a month to estimate living expenses and plan savings from each paycheck.
keyPoints.quote: Help your teen track what they actually spend in a month.

keyPoints.point: Students learn compound interest means earning interest on both saved money and previously earned interest, which grows faster when started early.
keyPoints.quote: Compound interest is when your child earns interest on both the money they save and the interest they earn.

keyPoints.point: Setting aside $100 every year starting at age 14 can grow to about $23,000 by age 65 at 5 percent, more than starting at age 35.
keyPoints.quote: If they set aside $100 every year starting at age 14, they'd have about $23,000 at age 65.

keyPoints.point: Some employers provide matching contributions for a 401(k) and it is smart to save enough to receive the maximum matching contribution.
keyPoints.quote: Some employers provide matching contributions as an incentive to save, so it’s smart to save at least enough for the maximum matching contribution.

keyTerms.gloss: Account where money is kept readily available for emergency expenses and can avoid high interest debt.
keyTerms.quote: Having money in a savings account can help your child avoid having to rely on credit cards

keyTerms.gloss: Interest earned on both the money saved and the interest previously earned.
keyTerms.quote: Compound interest is when your child earns interest on both the money they save and the interest they earn.

keyTerms.gloss: Money needed for monthly living expenses that determines the size of emergency savings.
keyTerms.quote: have at least three months’ worth of living expenses saved up in case of an emergency

keyTerms.gloss: Workplace retirement account where employers sometimes offer matching contributions as an incentive to save.
keyTerms.quote: Explain to your child that once they start a job, they may be offered a retirement account at work called a 401(k).

keyTerms.gloss: Protection for money kept in a bank or credit union that is federally insured as a safe place.
keyTerms.quote: Talk about how to keep money in a safe place, like a federally insured bank or credit union.
